subject: Planned: non-blocking live kernel patch in eastus3 — scheduling & opt-out
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmecorp.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: Planned: non-blocking live kernel patch in eastus3 — scheduling & opt-out

Hi Sarah / Acme ops team,

We have a planned, non-blocking kernel livepatch for the eastus3 host pool on Thursday 2027-12-16 between 02:00 and 06:00 UTC. This livepatch uses vendor-provided livepatching (no node reboots expected) and is targeted to address a kernel CVE that improves I/O scheduler behavior under high connection churn.

What to expect:
- No scheduled restarts. Hosts will remain online.
- Small, short-lived RPC latency spikes possible during the patch application (usually < 250ms, rare spikes to ~500ms).
- We will run a small canary cohort (5% of your traffic) for the first 30 minutes; if metrics hold we’ll roll the remainder.

Action items for Acme:
1) Please confirm by EOD Monday 2027-12-13 whether you want to: opt into the default window, request a different window, or opt-out entirely (we will postpone for you).
2) If you want to participate in the canary cohort, reply with the service names / API routes you prefer included.

Attachments: runbook + impact matrix attached for your SRE team. Runbook includes rollback and connection drain steps. Live link: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/runbooks/eastus3-livepatch

If you prefer a dedicated maintenance channel we can spin up a private Slack thread and an on-call rotation from our side.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmecorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, ops@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned: non-blocking live kernel patch in eastus3 — scheduling & opt-out

Thanks Karthik — quick clarifying questions:
1) Our platform has a P95 tail-sensitive endpoint (payments.checkout). Can you confirm the expected P95 delta during canary? You mentioned typical spikes but we need a tighter estimate.
2) Will the canary include any hosts that are currently pinned for our dedicated pool? We have a small subset of pinned hosts for latency-sensitive traffic.
3) We’d like to opt into the canary, but prefer the canary to run starting at 02:30 UTC (to finish an upstream batch job). Is that possible?

Also can you share the portion of the runbook covering quick rollback steps that our on-call can run if we see degradation?

—Sarah
Sarah Liu
Platform Reliability Lead
Acme Corp

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned: non-blocking live kernel patch in eastus3 — scheduling & opt-out

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick reply and great questions. Short answers:
- Expected P95 delta during canary: in our prior tests the P95 increased by ~45ms on heavily loaded tenants; typical production impact we’ve seen is 20–60ms during the 2–5 minute application windows. We will monitor the payments.checkout route specifically during canary and can abort early.
- Pinned hosts: your pinned hosts will be excluded from the automatic canary unless you explicitly ask us to include them. By default we’ll select ephemeral hosts from your shared pool.
- Canary start: 02:30 UTC is fine — we can shift the canary window to 02:30–03:00 and then proceed if metrics are green.

Attached I’ve pasted the rollback checklist excerpt below (also in runbook):
1) Pause livepatch rollout (control plane hold).
2) Evict canary hosts from the pool and re-route traffic to healthy hosts (we’ll coordinate).
3) Re-probe kernel version and restore connection scheduling parameters (automation script run: restore_sched.sh).
4) Open postmortem: tag services and notify affected product owners.

I’ll add a dedicated Slack channel and invite your on-call; Monica will own the on-call rotation from our side.

–Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior SRE, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acmecorp.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Dec 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-maintenance: eastus3 livepatch complete — summary & follow-ups

Hi all — quick post-maintenance summary for Acme and internal ops: 

What happened:
- Livepatch applied across eastus3 on 2027-12-16 starting 02:30 UTC; canary (5%) ran 02:30–03:00 UTC then rolled to remaining hosts 03:00–04:10 UTC.
- No host reboots were performed.
- Observed transient P95 increases on payments.checkout during canary: +52ms (peak 180ms) for a 3-minute stretch; metrics returned to baseline after rollout continued.
- We triggered a control-plane hold at 03:05 UTC for 12 minutes when a different tenant experienced a network interruption; we aborted additional rollouts for that tenant and resumed after verification.

Customer impact:
- Acme saw the transient P95 blip described above; no errors or retries were observed at the application layer.

Actions & next steps:
1) Postmortem document: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/postmortems/2027-12-eastus3-livepatch (draft). We’ll tag Acme’s SRE and include timeline + metric graphs.
2) Follow-up: Monica will share the canary telemetry pack (CSV) and the extracted impact matrix to the Acme maintenance Slack channel.
3) Preventative: we’re adding an automated pre-rollout probe for high-tail payment endpoints to block rollouts that exceed a 40ms expected P95 delta.

If you want a deeper timeline or raw logs for your internal postmortem, reply and we’ll package everything for you.

Thanks for coordinating — and thanks to Naomi & Monica for the quick response during the hold.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
